newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan PM Hashimoto's support rising - polls.
newsitem.headline: Japan PM Hashimoto's support rising - polls.

text.p: Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto's public support rating rose after he appointed his new cabinet last week, according to three opinion polls published by Japanese dailies on Sunday.

A poll by the Asahi Shimbun said 55 percent of respondents supported Hashimoto, while similar surveys by the Nihon Keizai Shimbun put his support rating at 50.9 percent and Yomiuri Shimbun at 56.6 percent.
The Asahi interviewed 2,000 adults by telephone on Friday and Saturday soon after Hashimoto formed his new cabinet only of members from his Liberal Democratic Party (LDP).
The Nihon Keizai telephone survey of 3,000 eligible voters was conducted in the same period while Yomiuri asked 1,500 voters.
Hashimoto's new cabinet was slightly more popular than the old coalition cabinet which he led, the surveys showed.
The long-awaited promises of administrative reform was high on the list of expectations among those polled, the Asahi said.
More than 53% of Asahi respondents believed that the new Hashimoto cabinet would carry out the reforms.
The Nikkei survey showed 46 percent of respondents felt reform should be a key task of his new cabinet.

The Nikkei survey also pointed to strong public dissatisfaction with the new electoral system under which the October 20 general elections were fought, with 77 percent saying they supported an overhaul.

The Lower House elections were the first to use a new voting system in which 300 lawmakers were selected in single-seat constituencies and 200 through proportional representation in 11 regional blocs.

Single-seat district candidates were also able to run in the proportional representation domain and some who lost in their single-seat constituencies actually won seats through proportional representation.
